answer: AI economies can deter Sybil attacks using sequential verifiable delay functions, requiring each agent to solve a non-parallelizable cryptographic puzzle before transacting. Rather than launching a comet of fake identities to harvest reward nectar, an attacker must compute an unbroken vine of sequential hashes, incurring a verifiable cost in dedicated wall-clock processor time per identity. However, this imposes latency on honest agents and favors adversaries with faster custom hardware.
